The only change is in the test file provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Startup/StartupPreloadTests.swift at line 885. The test-only stub NoEvictStubLanguageModel.prepare signature moves from (input, cache, windowSize) to (input, cache, state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters). This tracks an upstream LanguageModel protocol change. The stub returns .tokens(input.text) and has no security-relevant behavior.

This is test code and is not shipped in the provider artifact. It does not touch the coordinator WebSocket contract (TB-002), key custody, attestation (TB-009/TB-011), the SSD prefix cache (T-041), or authorization. No production control is weakened and no new attack surface is added, so I found no regression.

Unverified: the production LanguageModel protocol and prefill-parameter changes live in other files that were not supplied. The production callers of prepare, and any change to prefill windowing or KV or prefix-cache behavior, may sit in the same PR. A later pass should check that those changes preserve cacheSalt scoping and the KV memory admission and headroom logic that these startup tests exercise. This unit only shows the stub signature update.
